title: Two-Tiered Triage Guidance System
source_document: English Master Data Collection & Clinical Content Repository

content.text: Tier 1 signs require seeking immediate medical assistance / calling 112.
🚨 Tier 1: Emergency Warning Signs (Seek Immediate Medical Assistance / Call 112)

items: Autonomic Dysreflexia Signs: Sudden severe pounding headache, sweating/flushing above injury level, goosebumps, cold clammy skin below injury, or sudden blood pressure spike.
Acute Respiratory Distress: Severe shortness of breath, inability to clear secretions, cyanosis (bluish tint to lips/skin), or acute chest pain.
Severe Infection / Possible Systemic Urosepsis: High fever, chills, confusion, or dark/foul-smelling urine accompanied by systemic malaise.
Possible DVT / PE: Sudden unilateral leg swelling, warmth, redness, or acute shortness of breath and chest pain.

content.text: 🩺 Tier 2: Contact Healthcare Professional (Routine / Urgent Consultation)

items: Skin Redness or Breakdown: Non-blanchable red spots or early skin changes (Stage 1/2 skin injury).

Urinary Appearance Changes or Potential UTI: Changes in urine clarity/odor (note: urine appearance changes alone are not standalone proof of UTI), increased spasticity, low-grade fever, autonomic changes, or flank discomfort warranting clinical evaluation.
Bowel Changes: Persistent constipation or routine disruptions.
Worsening Spasms or Pain: Increases in spasticity, neuropathic pain, or joint discomfort.

source_notes: The warning line above the Tier 1 heading summarizes the heading's own instruction (Seek Immediate Medical Assistance / Call 112); the heading itself is the original source wording.
